extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders (unions, employers, attorneys, advocacy groups, members of the public) submitting comments to NLRB rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments on National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) rulemakings, including procedural requirements, substantive citation expectations, and topic areas commonly addressed. Intended to help commenters maximize legal and empirical relevance to the Board and rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments should be submitted either electronically to regulations.gov or by mail/hand-delivery to the NLRB Executive Secretary at the specified address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the two accepted delivery methods (regulations.gov or physical mail/hand-delivery to Roxanne L. Rothschild, Executive Secretary, National Labor Relations Board, 1015 Half Street S.E., Washington, D.C. 20570-0001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and reply comment scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply comments should be limited to replying to comments previously filed by other parties. No late comments will be accepted. Requests for extensions of time will be granted only for good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timeliness; use reply comments only for rebuttal to other commenters' factual claims or arguments; do not attempt to introduce new, non-responsive material in late filings or in reply comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific NLRA statutory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: For National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) rules: cite specific NLRA sections (29 USC §§ 151-169).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground legal arguments in the relevant NLRA provisions by citing exact U.S. Code sections to show statutory fit or conflict with proposed rule language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference relevant CFR provisions being amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference 29 CFR provisions being amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and cite the exact Code of Federal Regulations sections targeted by the rulemaking to make clear how proposed changes interact with existing regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Board precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with Board precedent (citing case names and citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss prior NLRB decisions, providing case names and citations to demonstrate how precedent supports or undercuts the commenter's position; address relevant reasoning and holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite federal court of appeals precedent reviewing Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite federal court of appeals cases reviewing Board decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appellate decisions that interpret or review NLRB rulings to bolster arguments about legal error, deference, or broader judicial trends affecting the Board's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide industry-specific empirical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide industry-specific data on union representation and collective bargaining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply sector- or industry-level statistics and factual information to show how the rule would play out in particular contexts (e.g., union density, bargaining coverage, historical trends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address differential impacts on employer types
rubrics_metrics.description: Address impact on different employer types (small business, healthcare, educational, federal contractors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed rule would affect particular employer categories, including any disproportionate burdens or sector-specific operational concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Bureau of Labor Statistics union data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use BLS statistics to support empirical claims about union membership, representation trends, and labor market conditions; cite specific BLS series or reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with right-to-work law interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with right-to-work law interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how state-level right-to-work laws might interact with the proposed rule and affect implementation, enforcement, or statutory interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address gig economy/platform worker NLRA coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Address gig economy / platform worker NLRA coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether and how the proposed rule affects independent contractors or platform/gig workers, including tests for employee status under the NLRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite other relevant statutes (Taft-Hartley, Landrum-Griffin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite the Taft-Hartley Act and Landrum-Griffin Act provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring in related statutory frameworks (e.g., Taft-Hartley, Landrum-Griffin) when they bear on the rule's legal context or constraints; provide section citations and explain relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election procedures as a comment topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Election procedures (representation petition handling, voter eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing election rules, focus on procedural handling of representation petitions, voter eligibility determinations, and related mechanics that affect election fairness and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint employer standard as a comment topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint employer standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss legal tests and factual standards for joint-employer status and how rule language will change or clarify employer liability and bargaining obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent contractor status under the NLRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent contractor status under NLRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze criteria for distinguishing employees from independent contractors and the implications for NLRA coverage under the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property access rights for organizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Property access rights for organizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how rules affect organizers' access to employer property and the balance between property rights and organizing protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union dues collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Union dues collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider rules that affect how unions collect dues, agency fees, or financial arrangements with members and nonmembers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and trade secret protection in elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality and trade secret protection in elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate protections for confidential employer information and trade secrets in the context of representation proceedings and evidence disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail vs. in-person ballot procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail vs. in-person ballot procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the consequences of alternate balloting methods for electoral integrity, access, and logistical feasibility; provide empirical or case-based support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bargaining unit determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Bargaining unit determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss criteria for defining appropriate bargaining units and the practical impacts of unit configuration on collective bargaining outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective bargaining duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective bargaining duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address scope and limits of the duty to bargain, mandatory subjects, and exceptions as affected by the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair labor practice charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfair labor practice charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how rule changes would affect the processing, standards, or remedies associated with unfair labor practice allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for Board precedent shifts between administrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board oscillates between administrations - effective comments engage with both prior precedent and current Board's stated rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate shifts in legal reasoning by addressing both historical and recent precedent and by framing arguments that are persuasive under competing interpretive approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider three-member quorum and timing effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-member quorum requirements affect rule timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge procedural constraints (e.g., quorum composition) that may influence implementation timelines or the Board's ability to act; use timing considerations strategically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reply comments to rebut factual claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply comment opportunity is unique - rebut other commenters' factual claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reply comments, focus on contesting factual assertions or evidence submitted by others rather than introducing wholly new claims; provide targeted counter-evidence or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address empirical implications for election rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Election rules have particular fact-intensive empirical implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply rigorous empirical analysis, data, or case studies when commenting on election-related rule changes, as these issues turn heavily on facts and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame arguments for variable Board panel composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Board panel composition can affect interpretation - frame for both sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft arguments that will be persuasive regardless of likely panel leanings by addressing alternative readings and emphasizing neutral statutory or evidentiary bases.
